name: Dataspace-federated DPP (Catena-X / Eclipse Tractus-X: DSP connectors, DCP credentials, AAS Digital Twin Registry, SAMM aspect models)
scope_note: Covers the dataspace-federated way to provide and consume product passports as practised in the Catena-X automotive dataspace and its Eclipse Tractus-X open-source reference stack: the Eclipse Dataspace Protocol (DSP 2025-1) and the Decentralized Claims Protocol (DCP 1.0.x), the Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC) connector and the Tractus-X EDC distribution (EDR tokens, ODRL policies), the central discovery services (Discovery Finder, BPN Discovery, EDC Discovery), the decentralized Digital Twin Registry built on the IDTA AAS Part 2 registry and discovery API, SAMM aspect models and the files ESMF generates from them, the Catena-X standards that bind these parts for the DPP use case (CX-0143, preview CX-0160), and the test kits (DSP TCK, DCP TCK, DPS TCK) and the Catena-X conformity assessment process. Gaia-X and Factory-X/Manufacturing-X appear as context only. Left out: the AAS family itself beyond its registry/discovery role (see the AAS method file), VC/SSI wallets beyond DCP, GS1 resolvers, EU registry operations, and the text of any EN, ISO, IEC or DIN document (rule 5: bibliographic data only). EU law statements reuse the prior substantive records of 2026-10-13 because EUR-Lex returned empty bodies on 2026-10-19.
summary: In this method a passport is not a public web document but a data asset that the economic operator keeps behind its own dataspace connector. Each participant runs a connector (in Catena-X the Tractus-X distribution of the Eclipse Dataspace Components) that speaks the Eclipse Dataspace Protocol 2025-1: a catalog protocol to list datasets with ODRL offers, a contract negotiation state machine, and a transfer process state machine, all as JSON-LD messages over HTTPS. Participants authenticate with the Decentralized Claims Protocol: a self-issued JWT bound to a DID, plus verifiable presentations of dataspace credentials (membership, BPN, framework agreement) fetched from a credential service. The provider registers a digital twin for each product (type or instance level) in its own Digital Twin Registry, which implements the IDTA AAS Part 2 registry and discovery profiles and is itself offered as a DSP dataset. Each twin lists specificAssetIds (manufacturerId, manufacturerPartId, partInstanceId, digitalTwinType) and submodel descriptors whose semanticId names a SAMM aspect model (for example the generic Digital Product Passport or the IDTA/Catena-X battery passport parts) and whose endpoint carries subprotocol DSP with the dataset id and the provider control-plane address. A consumer that holds a QR payload of the Tractus-X form CX:<manufacturerPartId>:<partInstanceId> first asks the Discovery Finder and BPN Discovery for the owner BPN, then the EDC Discovery for that BPN's connector address, reads /.well-known/dspace-version to choose the DSP version, requests the catalog filtered on the Digital Twin Registry type, negotiates a contract, and receives an Endpoint Data Reference (an HTTP endpoint plus a short-lived bearer token) in the TransferStartMessage. With that token it calls the registry through the provider data plane, looks up the twin by specificAssetIds, reads the passport submodel descriptor, negotiates a second contract for the submodel dataset, and finally GETs the aspect payload (JSON value-only serialization) through the data plane. Access tiers are realised by credential-based access policies in the connector, by BPN-based visibility rules in the registry (Edc-Bpn header injected by the provider connector, PUBLIC_READABLE only for selected keys), and by usage policies that must carry the framework agreement and the usage purpose cx.circular.dpp:1. Semantics come from SAMM models in Turtle, from which ESMF generates JSON Schema, OpenAPI, AAS submodel templates, sample payloads and documentation. The architecture deliberately has no public anonymous access path: the preview battery-passport standard CX-0160 itself states that a proxy outside the dataspace is needed to bridge Catena-X passports to the public EU DPP system and registry. The original Tractus-X Digital Product Pass consumer app is archived and deprecated; the Industry Core Hub is the recommended successor and still parses the CX triplet QR form.

maturity.adoption_evidence: Production use is limited to the Catena-X association's onboarded members; no public deployment count was found. Evidence seen: the Tractus-X reference stack is actively maintained (Tractus-X EDC, DTR, EDC Connector, DSP/DCP TCK repositories pushed in October 2026); Catena-X runs a third-party conformity assessment with four named conformity assessment bodies (TUEV SUED, Deloitte, TUEV Rheinland, SQS) under a CAF Handbook release Saturn (minor release Titan). The tractusx-edc multi-dataspace decision record of 2026-01-07 names Factory-X, Construct-X and Semiconductor-X as further dataspaces that want the same connector midstream. Counter-evidence of maturity for the DPP use case: the Tractus-X Digital Product Pass consumer app was deprecated for lack of maintenance and archived; the battery passport standard CX-0160 is only in the preview release; three different DPP aspect versions are named by the KIT (5.0.0), the standard (6.1.0) and the model repository (7.0.0). Academic evidence is prototype-level: an EDC-based DPP transfer prototype (Hulea et al. 2025), EDC/AAS integration comparisons with Catena-X and Factory-X prototypes (Schmidt et al. 2025), and Catena-X digital-twin lifecycle and circular-economy studies (Manoury et al. 2025; Muegge et al. 2023).
maturity.regulatory_alignment: Own reading against prior substantive law records (2026-10-13; not re-fetched this session). Strong fit: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(d) asks for open standards, interoperable formats and transfer through an open interoperable data exchange network without vendor lock-in; DSP and DCP are Apache-2.0 open specifications with an open TCK. Art. 11(f) and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 78(f) restrict who may introduce or modify data by access rights; the connector policy model and DTR write roles support this. Art. 11(g) and Art. 78(g) ask for authentication, reliability and integrity; DCP gives authenticated participants, but passports are not signed as documents. Weak fit: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(2)(a) and Art. 78(b), and Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 11(b), require free access for the public to the public part; the Catena-X architecture admits only onboarded participants with membership credentials, and CX-0160-3 section 5.2 (preview) itself calls for a bridge outside the dataspace. Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 2 defines the unique product identifier as also enabling a web link to the passport, and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(3) makes the QR code link to a unique identifier; the Tractus-X carrier payload CX:<manufacturerPartId>:<partInstanceId> is not a web link and needs a discovery chain plus credentials. Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(4) (backup copy through a DPP service provider) and Art. 11(e) / Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 78(e) (availability after the operator ceases activity) are not addressed by the peer-to-peer model, in which the passport is reachable only while the provider connector runs; the DPP 7.0.0 aspect carries a backupReference field but no mechanism. Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 13 and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(10) (upload of identifiers to the EU registry) have no Catena-X counterpart; the DPP 7.0.0 aspect has a registrationIdentifier field.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: Participants are identified twice: by a DID (CX-0018 v4.2 section 2.1.1 requires a DID in every DSP message property that identifies a participant; DCP self-issued tokens carry iss = sub = participant DID, aud = verifier DID) and by a Business Partner Number (CX-0010 v3.0.1): prefix 'BPN', a type character L (legal entity), S (site) or A (address), ten upper-case alphanumeric entity characters and two check characters, example BPNL00000000IF61 (written with spaces in the standard). The BPN still drives discovery (BPN Discovery, EDC Discovery), DTR visibility (externalSubjectId = BPN) and the BusinessPartnerNumber/BusinessPartnerGroup policy constraints; the Tractus-X connector resolves BPN to DID via a separate directory (connector-discovery extension, decision record 2026-01-07 names BDRS). Products are identified by AAS twin ids (urn:uuid), globalAssetId (urn:uuid in examples) and specificAssetIds: manufacturerId (BPNL), manufacturerPartId (type-level part number), partInstanceId (serial, unique only as agreed between provider and consumer, per CX-0160 base 2.1.1), customerPartId (optional), digitalTwinType = PartInstance or PartType (mandatory since CX-0143 v1.4.0 2.1.4.3). The DPP aspect carries its own passportIdentifier with a UUID pattern (plain UUID or urn:uuid:) in metadata (DPP aspect 7.0.0 JSON Schema). Assets in the connector have their own @id; the submodel dataset id is referenced from subprotocolBody 'id=' and SHOULD be a UUIDv4 (CX-0143 2.1.4.3).

L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 2 and Art. 10(1)(a)-(c) bind the passport to a persistent unique product identifier that also enables a web link; the Catena-X keys are composite, scoped to the manufacturer BPN, and not web links. Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(3) names the ISO/IEC 15459 series for the unique identifier (bibliographic only); whether a CX triplet or a urn:uuid twin id satisfies that cannot be judged without the protected text. Operator identifiers: the BPN is a private Catena-X scheme; Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 12(1) points to the standards listed in Annex III for unique operator identifiers (not examined here).

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: No Catena-X standard read in this session fixes a carrier or payload. The Tractus-X reference practice encodes plain text CX:<manufacturerPartId>:<partInstanceId> in a QR code: the archived Digital Product Pass app tutorial tells users to generate a text QR code of that form, and the Industry Core Hub passport QR scanner validates the decoded text with the regular expression ^CX:[^:]+:[^:]+$ before discovery. The DPP aspect (5.0.0 to 7.0.0) records carrier metadata inside the passport: identification.dataCarriers[] with carrierType (for example 'QR') and carrierPositions; the EcoPass KIT example shows carrierType QR and a layout position text. The battery passport parts in CX-0160 (preview) do not define a carrier.

L02_data_carriers.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 13(6) and Art. 77(3) require a QR code that gives access to the battery passport through a unique identifier; Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(a)-(b) require a data carrier physically present on the product, packaging or documents connected to a persistent unique product identifier. L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: Three protocol layers. (1) Discovery (Catena-X central services, plain HTTPS JSON, not behind a connector): Discovery Finder POST {base}/api/{version}/administration/connectors/discovery/search returns BPN Discovery endpoints for a key type (for example manufacturerPartId; CX-0143 2.1.4.2 uses type 'mpn'); BPN Discovery POST .../administration/connectors/bpnDiscovery/search with body {searchFilter:[{type, keys[]}]} returns {bpns:[{type,key,value(BPN),resourceId}]}; registration via POST .../bpnDiscovery (and /batch, DELETE /{resourceId}); EDC Discovery POST /api/administration/connectors/discovery with a JSON array of BPNLs returns [{bpn, connectorEndpoint[]}] (CX-0001 v1.2.1 section 3.1). (2) Dataspace Protocol 2025-1 HTTPS binding, all messages application/json, JSON-LD context https://w3id.org/dspace/2025/1/context.jsonld (terms @protected), JSON Schemas normative: GET {root}/.well-known/dspace-version (MUST be unversioned and unauthenticated; body {protocolVersions:[{version, path, binding:'HTTPS', serviceId?, identifierType?, auth?:{protocol, version, profile[]}}]}, schema protocol-version-schema.json, draft 2019-09, required version/path/binding); catalog POST {base}/catalog/request (CatalogRequestMessage with optional filter; unsupported filter gives 400), GET {base}/catalog/datasets/{id}; pagination by HTTP Link headers rel next/previous; optional gzip. Contract negotiation provider paths GET /negotiations/{providerPid}, POST /negotiations/request (201 Created), POST /negotiations/{providerPid}/request|events|agreement/verification|termination; consumer callback paths /negotiations/offers, /{callback}/negotiations/{consumerPid}/offers|agreement|events|termination; states REQUESTED, OFFERED, ACCEPTED, AGREED, VERIFIED, FINALIZED, TERMINATED. Transfer process provider paths GET /transfers/{providerPid}, POST /transfers/request (201), /transfers/{providerPid}/start|completion|termination|suspension; consumer callbacks /{callback}/transfers/{consumerPid}/start|completion|termination|suspension; states REQUESTED, STARTED, SUSPENDED, COMPLETED, TERMINATED; invalid transition gives 400, unknown or unauthorized process gives 404. Pull transfers return a DataAddress in TransferStartMessage. Connectors MAY advertise DataService/CatalogService entries in their DID document service array. (3) Catena-X profile (CX-0018 v4.2): DSP 2025-1 mandatory, legacy key 'v0.8' (and tolerance for '0.8') in version metadata; version endpoint at https://<host>/<subpath>/.well-known/dspace-version advertised in the DID document as service type DataService; transfer types HttpData-PULL, AmazonS3-PUSH, AzureStorage-PUSH. For HttpData-PULL the TransferStartMessage dataAddress MUST use endpointType https://w3id.org/idsa/v4.1/HTTP with endpointProperties https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/endpoint (REQUIRED), .../authorization (REQUIRED, used unchanged in the Authorization header), .../authType (OPTIONAL), https://w3id.org/tractusx/auth/refreshEndpoint and refreshToken (OPTIONAL, refresh per RFC 6749 section 6 with an STS token), https://w3id.org/tractusx/auth/expiresIn (REQUIRED). Tractus-X EDC exposes the result to the consumer backend as an Endpoint Data Reference: management API POST /v3/edrs (negotiate and auto-transfer, protocol 'dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1', counterPartyAddress like https://provider/api/v1/dsp/2025-1), POST /v3/edrs/request (query), GET /v3/edrs/{transferProcessId}/dataaddress?auto_refresh=true, POST /v3/edrs/{id}/refresh; data fetch GET {endpoint}/{subpath} with header Authorization: <token>; or consumer proxy POST {consumer-dataplane}/proxy/aas/request with {assetId, providerId, pathSegments, queryParams}. Connector discovery helper POST /v3/connectordiscovery/connectors {counterPartyId: did} and /v3/connectordiscovery/dspversionparams.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.observable_black_box: Without dataspace credentials: the version metadata endpoint (unauthenticated by rule), the DID document service entries, the HTTP status of DSP endpoints (404 is the mandated answer to unauthorized access), the central discovery service APIs if they are reachable. With credentials: catalog content and ODRL offers, negotiation and transfer state transitions, the EDR dataAddress and its token lifetime, and finally the passport payload. Sample artifacts (catalog JSON, TransferStartMessage, EDR) can be checked offline against the DSP JSON Schemas and contexts.
L03_data_exchange_protocols.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(d) and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(5) ask for transfer through an open interoperable data exchange network without vendor lock-in; DSP is an open Apache-2.0 specification, but participation in Catena-X requires membership credentials and Catena-X standards are published as all-rights-reserved documents. Neither law prescribes a negotiation step; the contract negotiation before each read is an addition.

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: Search and read go through the Digital Twin Registry (AAS Part 2 registry and discovery interfaces, IDTA 01002 v3.2 referenced by CX-0002 v2.4.0). Data providers MUST offer the Registry Minimal Read profile SSP-005 and the Discovery Read profile SSP-002, SHOULD offer the Query profile SSP-004, MAY offer the Full profile SSP-001 (create/delete) and the Bulk profile; paths SHOULD carry only the major version (/v3/); unsupported operations or parameter values MUST answer 501 (CX-0002 2.1.5, 3.1.2). Tractus-X DTR 0.13.0 OpenAPI: GET/POST /shell-descriptors, GET/PUT/DELETE /shell-descriptors/{aasIdentifier}, GET/POST /shell-descriptors/{aasIdentifier}/submodel-descriptors, GET/PUT/DELETE .../submodel-descriptors/{submodelIdentifier}, GET /description, GET /lookup/shells?assetIds=<base64url SpecificAssetId JSON>&limit&cursor&createdAfter (deprecated), POST /lookup/shellsByAssetLink?limit&cursor[&createdAfter] with body of {name, value} pairs, GET/POST/DELETE /lookup/shells/{aasIdentifier}, private POST /submodel-descriptor/authorized; identifiers in paths are UTF-8 base64url encoded; paging by cursor and paging_metadata; createdAfter in RFC 3339 is a Tractus-X extension (CX-0160 base 1.4.1 notes CX-0002 2.3.0 did not require it). The registry itself is offered as a DSP dataset with dct:type {'@id': https://w3id.org/catenax/taxonomy#DigitalTwinRegistry} and cx-common:version >= '3.0' (deprecated asset:prop:type 'data.core.digitalTwinRegistry' MAY remain). Passport payloads are served by a submodel server under the Submodel Service Specification Value Profile SSP-003: consumers call the descriptor href with GET; for interface 'SUBMODEL-3.x' they append /$value, for 'SUBMODEL-VALUE-3.x' they use href as is; operations /serialization, $metadata-style modifiers and Level=Core are not supported in that profile (CX-0002 4.1, 5). Submodel datasets carry dct:type https://w3id.org/catenax/taxonomy#Submodel and SHOULD carry aas-semantics:semanticId. CX-0143 4.1.1 fixes the EDC asset shape for passports (dataAddress type HttpData, baseUrl of the submodel server, proxyPath/proxyQueryParams/proxyMethod/proxyBody 'true'). Lifecycle writes (create, update, deactivate) are provider-internal: provider updates the twin or submodel in its own DTR and submodel server; CX-0160 base 4.2 and 5.1.4 (preview) add optional event notifications (CreateSubmodel events under CX-0151) and bulk retrieval of new instance twins via createdAfter. No deactivate or archive operation for passports is standardised; the DPP aspect carries passportStatus.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: Payload semantics are SAMM aspect models written in RDF/Turtle (SAMM 2.2.0 latest; Catena-X models use the urn:samm:org.eclipse.esmf.samm:meta-model:2.1.0# namespaces), validated with SHACL shapes in ESMF. Model element ids are URNs urn:samm:<namespace>:<version>#<Element>, for example urn:samm:io.catenax.generic.digital_product_passport:7.0.0#DigitalProductPassport; older twins in examples still use urn:bamm:... ids. ESMF samm-cli (2.16.x) generates from one model: JSON Schema ('to schema'; the published DPP 7.0.0 schema declares draft-04 and uses boolean exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum inside components.schemas), OpenAPI 3.0.3 YAML/JSON ('to openapi'; DPP 7.0.0 OpenAPI path /{tenant-id}/digital-product-passport with server catenax.io/api/v7), AsyncAPI, example JSON payload ('to json'), Apache Parquet sample, JSON-LD, HTML documentation, PNG/SVG diagrams, SQL (Databricks dialect), Java classes, and AAS submodel templates in XML, JSON or AASX ('to aas'); the sldt-semantic-models gen/ folder ships -schema.json, .yml, .json, .html, -aas.xml, .aasx and .parquet per model. The generic DPP aspect 7.0.0 has top-level properties metadata, identification, operation, handling, characteristics, commercial, sustainability, sources, additionalData (optional), compliances, composition; metadata holds version, passportStatus (enum draft, approved, invalid, expired), issueDate and expirationDate (YYYY-MM-DD), passportIdentifier (UUID), predecessor, backupReference, registrationIdentifier, lastModification, language, economicOperator, specVersion. The battery pass 6.1.0 aspect reuses DPP 5.0.0 metadata/commercial/handling. CX-0143 v1.4.0 mandates DPP 6.1.0 (idShort digitalProductPass) and Transmission Pass 3.1.0 (idShort transmissionPass); CX-0160 (preview) moves batteries to seven joint IDTA/Catena-X models io.admin-shell.idta.batterypass.{digital_nameplate, handover_documentation, carbon_footprint, technical_data, product_condition, material_composition, circularity}:1.0.x, split between PartType and PartInstance twins, plus urn:samm:io.admin-shell.idta.dpp.dpp_metadata:1.0.0#DppMetadata with supplemental semantic id https://admin-shell.io/idta/cds/dppMetadata/1. Protocol-level vocabularies: DSP context https://w3id.org/dspace/2025/1/context.jsonld and ODRL profile context https://w3id.org/dspace/2025/1/odrl-profile.jsonld; EDC namespace https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/; Tractus-X namespaces https://w3id.org/tractusx/v0.0.1/ns/ and https://w3id.org/tractusx/auth/; Catena-X policy context https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/context.jsonld and ODRL file https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/odrl.jsonld; taxonomy https://w3id.org/catenax/taxonomy#; ontology https://w3id.org/catenax/ontology/common#; credentials context https://w3id.org/catenax/credentials/v1.0.0; DCP context https://w3id.org/dspace-dcp/v1.0/dcp.jsonld.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Storage is decentralised by design: each provider keeps the passport in its own submodel server behind its own connector and DTR (CX-0143 1.2; CX-0002). Persistence is only as long as the provider runs these services; there is no Catena-X central copy, archive or escrow mechanism. The DPP aspect 7.0.0 metadata has backupReference (string) and the version/predecessor fields, so a provider can point to a backup copy and to an earlier passport, but no protocol defines how a backup is reached. The Industry Core Hub stores submodel data and registers the EDC asset on behalf of the provider. L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: Four stacked controls. (a) Participant authentication by DCP 1.0 (CX-0018 2.3): the consumer obtains a Self-Issued ID Token (JWT; iss = sub = own DID, aud = verifier DID, jti, exp, iat; optional token claim carrying an access token for the credential service) from its Secure Token Service and sends it in the Authorization header of each DSP message; the provider (verifier) resolves the DID document, checks a key with the capabilityInvocation relationship, then calls the consumer Credential Service POST {base}/presentations/query (PresentationQueryMessage with scopes such as org.eclipse.dspace.dcp.vc.type:<Type>) to obtain verifiable presentations; Catena-X catalog requests must be scoped to MembershipCredential, BPN credential and DataExchangeGovernance (framework agreement) credential (CX-0050). (b) Access policies (ODRL, action 'access') on contract definitions decide catalog visibility: BusinessPartnerNumber or BusinessPartnerGroup checked against the BPN from the credential, Membership, FrameworkAgreement. (c) Usage policies (action 'use') evaluated at negotiation: CX-0152 requires each usage policy to contain FrameworkAgreement and one UsagePurpose constraint chained with odrl:and, only constraints from the Catena-X policy schema, and the ODRL profile IRI https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/; CX-0143 4.1.2 and CX-0160 require UsagePurpose cx.circular.dpp:1 for passports (Tractus-X EDC lists 25+ allowed leftOperands such as UsagePurpose, ContractReference, DataUsageEndDate, AffiliatesBpnl). (d) Data-plane tokens: the EDR authorization token is short-lived (expiresIn, 300 s in the Tractus-X example) and refreshable; the provider data plane may still refuse requests outside the agreement. Inside the DTR, visibility of specificAssetIds is BPN-based: the provider EDC injects header Edc-Bpn with the consumer BPN; a specificAssetId is visible only to the owner and to BPNs listed in its externalSubjectId keys (closed by default); the wildcard PUBLIC_READABLE is allowed by default only for manufacturerPartId and assetLifecyclePhase (helm values registry.externalSubjectIdWildcardPrefix and ...AllowedTypes); read access to one specificAssetId grants read of the other twin fields, while PUBLIC_READABLE-only readers see a reduced field set; an alternative granular access-control mode uses rule sets (roles read_access_rules, write_access_rules, submodel_access_control). DTR technical clients use OAuth/OIDC (Keycloak or AWS Cognito) with RBAC roles. DSP error semantics hide existence: unauthorized requests for a negotiation or transfer MUST get 404.

With test credentials on a loopback dataspace: catalog filtering per BPN, policy rejection at negotiation, DTR responses that differ by Edc-Bpn header value, EDR expiry behaviour. L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(2) defines three access groups (public; notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission; persons with a legitimate interest) and Art. 78(b) requires free access per those rights; Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 11(b) requires free and easy access for listed actors. Catena-X has no public tier and no role for authorities that are not dataspace members; legitimate-interest roles would have to be modelled as BPN groups or custom credentials. The usage-purpose constraint cx.circular.dpp:1 refers to use under public law requiring passports (CX-0160 base 2.2, preview), which is an addition, not a legal requirement.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Integrity and authenticity are channel- and party-based, not document-based. TLS (HTTPS base URLs are mandatory in DSP and DCP) protects transport; DCP authenticates the requesting party with a DID-bound JWT whose signature is checked against the DID document key (kid header or single capabilityInvocation method), with replay protection by jti and expiry by exp; verifiable credentials follow DCP profiles vc20-bssl/jwt (VC Data Model 2.0, enveloped JOSE proofs, Bitstring Status List revocation) or vc11-sl2021/jwt (VC 1.1, external JWT proofs, StatusList2021); credentials and presentations must be homogeneous in model and proof; the concrete signature algorithm is not fixed by DCP. Catena-X credentials carry credentialStatus with statusListIndex and statusListCredential (CX-0050). The passport payload itself carries no signature in the Catena-X DPP or battery aspect models read here. The Tractus-X DPP Verification add-on (simple-wallet issuing aspect-model verifiable credentials for attribute certification) was a proof of concept inside the archived DPP app; its documentation moved to the Data Trust and Security KIT (not read).

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: Three versioning planes. Protocol: DSP versions are negotiated through /.well-known/dspace-version; Catena-X keeps v0.8 alongside 2025-1; Tractus-X promises strict backward compatibility within one DSP version only. Models: every aspect model change produces a new URN version (for example DPP 5.0.0, 6.0.0, 6.1.0, 7.0.0); CX-0143 has a backward-compatibility page and requires consumers to identify the semantic model version; metadata.specVersion and the battery specVersion example urn:io.catenax.battery.battery_pass:6.1.0 name the model inside the payload. Passports: the DPP aspect metadata carries version, passportStatus (draft, approved, invalid, expired), issueDate, expirationDate, lastModification and predecessor; updates are made in place by the provider; CX-0160 (preview) adds CreateSubmodel event notifications and createdAfter polling for new twins. Ownership change: Catena-X research compares approaches for digital-twin ownership change across lifecycles (Manoury et al.); no standardised handover protocol between operators was found. Battery status values (original, repurposed, re-used, remanufactured, waste) come from Annex XIII of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 and would sit in the battery models.

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Governance is association-based. Catena-X Automotive Network e.V. publishes the standards (release trains Jupiter, Io, Saturn, Titan current, Neptune preview), the operating model and rulebooks; participants sign the Catena-X terms and the Data Exchange Governance framework agreement and hold the corresponding credential. Roles in the standards: Data Provider/Consumer, Business Application Provider, Enablement Service Provider, Core Service Provider (CX-0001 Core Service Provider B runs participant-agent registration and the EDC Discovery API; Gaia-X style self-description documents MUST be created and registered at an SD storage), Onboarding Service Provider, Advisory Provider, Conformity Assessment Body. Conformity: business applications, enablement services and data providers/consumers are certified by nominated CABs (TUEV SUED, Deloitte, TUEV Rheinland, SQS) against conformity assessment criteria (CX-0143 ConformityAssessmentCriteria.md; CX-0160 CAC files with ids such as CX-0160-1-CAC-001 that review data offers and EDC assets); the CAF Handbook release Saturn (minor release Titan) governs; BPN conformity is by a self-audited signed declaration (CX-0010 1.3). Identity anchor: DIDs (CX-0049 DID document schema) and Catena-X credentials (CX-0050) issued by the operating company's issuer. Open-source stewardship: Eclipse Foundation (Dataspace Working Group for DSP/DCP and the TCKs; Eclipse Tractus-X for the reference stack; ESMF for SAMM). Context: Gaia-X trust framework (Architecture Document 25.11: compliance engine, registry, notaries, Digital Clearing Houses, wallets with OID4VC, Eclipse DCP or DIDComm) is named as a basis in older Catena-X papers; Factory-X/Manufacturing-X reuse the Tractus-X EDC midstream (factoryx-edc now archived).

end_to_end_flows.name: Carrier scan to passport payload inside Catena-X (consumer with membership)
actors: End user with consumer app (Industry Core Hub or archived DPP app)
Consumer connector (Tractus-X EDC) and its Secure Token Service and Credential Service
Provider connector control plane and data plane
steps: 1. Scan the QR code and decode text CX:<manufacturerPartId>:<partInstanceId>; check it against ^CX:[^:]+:[^:]+$ and split at ':' (IC-Hub practice).
2. POST Discovery Finder .../administration/connectors/discovery/search with the key type (manufacturerPartId; 'mpn' in CX-0143 examples) to get the BPN Discovery endpoint(s).
3. POST BPN Discovery .../administration/connectors/bpnDiscovery/search {searchFilter:[{type, keys:[<manufacturerPartId>]}]} and read bpns[].value (BPNL of the manufacturer).

4. POST EDC Discovery /api/administration/connectors/discovery with ["BPNL..."] and read connectorEndpoint[] (or resolve the provider DID and read its DataService service entry; Tractus-X helper POST /v3/connectordiscovery/connectors).
5. GET <connector root>/.well-known/dspace-version (no credentials) and pick 2025-1; build <base> = root + path.

6. Consumer obtains a Self-Issued ID Token from its STS scoped to Membership, BPN and DataExchangeGovernance credentials; provider will call the consumer Credential Service /presentations/query to verify.

7. Consumer control plane POSTs <base>/catalog/request (DSP) and filters datasets with dct:type https://w3id.org/catenax/taxonomy#DigitalTwinRegistry (legacy asset:prop:type data.core.digitalTwinRegistry).

8. Negotiate the DTR offer: POST <base>/negotiations/request with the offer copied unchanged plus assigner and target; states move REQUESTED to AGREED, VERIFIED, FINALIZED (Tractus-X POST /v3/edrs collapses negotiation and transfer).

9. POST <base>/transfers/request with format HttpData-PULL; provider answers TransferStartMessage whose dataAddress (endpointType https://w3id.org/idsa/v4.1/HTTP) carries endpoint, authorization token and expiresIn; the consumer caches it as an EDR.

10. Through the provider data plane with header Authorization: <token>, POST {dtr}/lookup/shellsByAssetLink with [{name:'manufacturerPartId'}, {name:'partInstanceId'}, {name:'digitalTwinType', value:'PartInstance'}] (the provider EDC adds Edc-Bpn = consumer BPN; DTR filters by externalSubjectId).

11. GET {dtr}/shell-descriptors/{base64url(aasId)}; select the submodel descriptor whose semanticId is the passport aspect URN (for example urn:samm:io.catenax.generic.digital_product_passport:6.1.0#DigitalProductPassport, idShort digitalProductPass).

12. Parse endpoints[].protocolInformation: subprotocol 'DSP', subprotocolBody 'id=<datasetId>;dspEndpoint=<provider control plane>', href = data plane URL plus submodel path, interface SUBMODEL-3.x or SUBMODEL-VALUE-3.x.

13. Catalog request filtered on the dataset id, negotiate the submodel offer whose usage policy holds FrameworkAgreement and UsagePurpose cx.circular.dpp:1, start an HttpData-PULL transfer and receive a second EDR.

14. GET href (+ '/$value' for SUBMODEL-3.x) with the second EDR token; the provider data plane proxies to the submodel server and returns the aspect JSON payload; refresh the token at refreshEndpoint when expiresIn passes.
15. Validate and render the payload against the generated JSON Schema (IC-Hub renders any draft-04+ schema).

end_to_end_flows.name: Provider publishes a passport (registration side)
actors: Economic operator (data provider) or business application provider
steps: 1. Produce the aspect payload conforming to the mandated SAMM model version; store it in the submodel server.

2. Create an EDC asset for the submodel (dataAddress type HttpData, baseUrl submodel server, proxyPath/proxyQueryParams/proxyMethod/proxyBody 'true'; dct:type taxonomy#Submodel, cx-common:version, aas-semantics:semanticId).

3. Create access and usage policy definitions (profile https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/; FrameworkAgreement and UsagePurpose cx.circular.dpp:1 chained with and) and a contract definition selecting the asset by id.

4. Register or update the twin in the DTR with specificAssetIds (manufacturerId, manufacturerPartId, partInstanceId, digitalTwinType), set externalSubjectId to consumer BPNs or PUBLIC_READABLE (manufacturerPartId only), and add the submodel descriptor (semanticId, idShort, DSP subprotocolBody, href).
5. Offer the DTR itself as a DSP dataset (dct:type taxonomy#DigitalTwinRegistry).
6. Register manufacturerPartId -> own BPN at BPN Discovery (POST .../bpnDiscovery {type, key}); the BPN comes from the caller token.
7. Publish the connector version endpoint in the DID document as a DataService entry and register the connector at the Core Service Provider for EDC Discovery.

end_to_end_flows.name: Bridge from Catena-X to the EU DPP system (CX-0160-3 section 5.2, preview concept)
actors: Economic operator or DPP service provider with a certified business application
EU-facing DPP management system outside Catena-X
steps: 1. Collect complete battery passport data on model and item level from suppliers through the Catena-X flows above.
2. Transfer the data from the operator back end to the EU-facing DPP management system; reject incomplete data sets.

3. That system registers the passport at the EU registry, offers a lifecycle API, a stable resolver endpoint, role-based access for restricted data and free public access (functions listed in the preview text; no technical profile given).

failure_modes.fault: manufacturerPartId contains ':' so the CX triplet splits into wrong parts.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Parse the decoded QR text and compare the split fields with the twin's specificAssetIds in a sample.

failure_modes.fault: partInstanceId is unique only per manufacturer, and two providers register the same manufacturerPartId at BPN Discovery.
failure_modes.detectable_by: BPN Discovery sample returning more than one BPN for one key; consistency check between carrier and twin manufacturerId.

failure_modes.fault: Version metadata endpoint requires authentication, omits 2025-1, or uses '0.8' where CX-0018 wants 'v0.8'.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Unauthenticated GET of /.well-known/dspace-version and schema plus rule checks.

failure_modes.fault: TransferStartMessage lacks expiresIn or uses a non-standard endpointType, so consumers cannot refresh or call the data plane.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Rule pack on TransferStartMessage/EDR samples.

failure_modes.fault: JSON-LD prefixes in policies resolve to unintended IRIs, so a constraint silently means something else.
failure_modes.detectable_by: data.context allowlist on samples; compare compacted terms with the expected expanded IRIs.

failure_modes.fault: DTR answers 404 or 500 instead of 501 for an unsupported profile operation, or only offers the deprecated GET /lookup/shells.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Contract test against the pinned DTR OpenAPI on a loopback instance.

failure_modes.fault: AAS ids in paths are not base64url encoded or are double encoded.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Request the same twin with correct and incorrect encodings and compare responses.

failure_modes.fault: Submodel descriptor uses an outdated semanticId (urn:bamm or an older DPP version), so consumers cannot identify the passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Rule on the descriptor semanticId against the mandated URN list.

failure_modes.fault: Payload validates against a different model version than its semanticId or specVersion states.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Validate against the schema chosen by the semanticId and compare with metadata.specVersion.

failure_modes.fault: partInstanceId (serial) flagged PUBLIC_READABLE through changed helm values, leaking instance data to every DTR reader.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Access probe with an unlisted BPN on a loopback DTR; canary specificAssetIds.

failure_modes.fault: DTR reachable directly (not only through the provider EDC), so any caller can set Edc-Bpn and impersonate a partner.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Direct request with a forged Edc-Bpn header to a deployment (loopback test environment only).

failure_modes.fault: Pure dataspace deployment offers no anonymous access to the public battery passport part.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Anonymous resolution from the carrier ends without a passport (identifier not resolvable).

failure_modes.fault: EDR token accepted after the transfer process was terminated or after expiresIn.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Replay of a captured TEST-ONLY token on a loopback provider after termination.

failure_modes.fault: Verifier accepts a self-issued token whose iss differs from sub or whose jti was used before.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Token mutation tests (dcp-tck verifier group or engine sample checks).

failure_modes.fault: passportStatus 'expired' or 'invalid' but the passport is still served without notice, or predecessor points to a non-existent passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Rule pack over payload sequences; predecessor lookup in the same SUT.

failure_modes.fault: Provider connector decommissioned; passport disappears with no backup route.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Scheduled re-acquisition over time (persistence.scheduled, not available today).

failure_modes.fault: No upload to the EU registry; registrationIdentifier empty.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Presence rule and mock registry comparison.

failure_modes.fault: Usage policy lacks UsagePurpose cx.circular.dpp:1 or chains constraints without odrl:and, so certified consumers cannot negotiate.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Rule pack on catalog offer samples.

failure_modes.fault: Consumer side still runs the archived Tractus-X DPP app with unmaintained dependencies.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Not a black-box observable; supply-chain review of the declared SUT components.

failure_modes.fault: Provider or consumer tooling validates passports with a 2020-12 or 2019-09 validator against the draft-04 SAMM-generated schema without conversion, so the schema is rejected or the boolean exclusive bounds are ignored and out-of-range values pass.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Validate boundary-value payloads (value equal to an exclusive bound) against a reviewed 2020-12 conversion; a SUT that accepts them shows the defect.

open_questions: Which generic DPP aspect version should the engine pin: 6.1.0 (mandated by CX-0143 v1.4.0 in CX-Titan), 7.0.0 (latest 'release' in sldt-semantic-models), or 5.0.0 (EcoPass KIT 26.09)? Battery passports move to the seven IDTA/Catena-X models only when CX-0160 leaves preview.
Is there any Catena-X or Tractus-X specification that maps a CX triplet to a public web URL, or a plan to use GS1 Digital Link or another URL form on the carrier? None was found.
Can BPN check characters be verified from an open source? CX-0010 delegates the algorithm to a protected ISO/IEC document.
Should the engine accept a signed DSP TCK or DCP TCK run as evidence through manual.review, given that both TCKs need a bidirectional, credentialed connection the engine does not make?
How should DSP '404 for unauthorized' be represented in the access-policy model, which treats only 401/403 as refusal?
What does the DSP tag 2025-1-RC5 (2026-08-31, after 2025-1-err1) mean for the stable 2025-1 line?
Will the Catena-X conformity assessment criteria for CX-0143 and CX-0160 be published as machine-checkable test cases? Only prose CAC files were seen; the CAF handbook PDF was not read.

Should the project accept a reviewed, pinned 2020-12 conversion of SAMM-generated draft-04 schemas and a locally bundled copy of the DSP schemas as fixtures? Both need a maintainer decision; neither was made.
anomalies: DSP root page redirect text calls the target 'the latest Release Candidate', while the target page 2025-1-err2 is titled 'Dataspace Protocol Release 2025-1' and says it is stable.
DSP tag order: 2025-1-err1 (2025-11-12), then 2025-1-RC5 (2026-08-31, pre-release), then 2025-1-err2 (2026-09-11) with the same terminology change.
DSP version schema lists '0.8' in its enum, while CX-0018 v4.2 requires the key 'v0.8'; both pass because the schema also allows any string.
Catena-X overview lists CX-0143 at 1.2.0; the live CX-0143 page and Titan source say v1.4.0.
CX-0050 has no version on the overview; Titan source heading says v.2.2.1. CX-0001 is now titled 'Participant Agent Registration' but still holds the EDC Discovery API.
CX-0002 v2.4.0 cites CX-0018 v4.1.1 in its non-normative references while CX-0018 is v4.2.
CX-0160 exists only in the CX-Neptune preview tree; CX-0143 (Titan) still refers to 'CX-XXXX Battery Passport'.
CX-0160-3 section 3.1.2 links the DPP Metadata specification artifacts to Digital Nameplate files (apparent copy error).
EcoPass KIT 26.09 names DPP 5.0.0, battery 6.0.0 and 'SAMM 1.1.0', which conflict with CX-0143 (6.1.0), the model repository (7.0.0) and the SAMM 2.1.0 namespaces in the models.
Tractus-X DTR OpenAPI is titled 'V3.1.0_SSP-001' while CX-0002 v2.4.0 references IDTA 01002 v3.2.
SAMM-generated JSON Schema of DPP 7.0.0 declares draft-04 and uses boolean exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum; the generated OpenAPI is 3.0.3 with server 'catenax.io/api/v7' (no scheme).
The Tractus-X Digital Product Pass app is archived and deprecated; its docs remain the most detailed public description of the consumer flow.
Tractus-X EDC multi-dataspace decision record (2026-01-07) cites the Factory-X EDC, which was archived on 2026-06-29.

Catena-X Titan certification page says 'Coming Soon' and the 'Conformity Assessment' navigation entry is commented out, while catena-x.net lists active CABs and a CAF handbook. One catena-x.net certification URL from search returned HTTP 404.
DCP dsp.profile.md links the DSP at the former IDSA GitHub location.
Manoury et al.: Consensus lists 2024 and 'Unknown Journal'; Crossref lists Procedia Computer Science 2025.
